LESSON: HUMAN RIGHTS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Human rights
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Human rights, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How could respect for human rights promote unity in society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Human rights together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Unity: learners collaborate with others as they use a chart in groups to illustrate categories of human rights and make a presentation

• Social justice: learners proactively solve problems as they engage with a resource person on ways in which human rights are violated in

society.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Assertiveness: as learners engage with a resource person on ways in which human rights are violated in society

• Self-awareness: as learners use digital/print resources to find out ways in which human rights are upheld in the society.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Religious Studies: as learners engage with a resource person on ways of promoting respect for human rights in the society.

• Creative Arts: learners role play scenarios that depict respect for human rights in the society.

Suggested learning Resources

Posters, print and digital resources, adapted learner’s books, resource persons, The Kenyan constitution, libraries,
